newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CPI SEEN UP, OUTPUT GROWTH SLOWER - ANALYST.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CPI SEEN UP, OUTPUT GROWTH SLOWER - ANALYST.

text.p: Polish prices will grow quicker in upcomming months than earlier expected, while industrial output growth will be lower, said Tadeusz Chroscicki, the chief analyst at the government's Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS).

In his macroeconomic forecast, submitted monthly to Reuters, Chroscicki said that year-on-year inflation would rise to 18.6 percent at the end of the first quarter, up from last month's forecast of 18.0 percent.
In January the year-on-year index fell to 18.1 percent after ending 1996 at 18.5 percent.
Chroscicki pared his industrial growth foecast by one point to a nine percent average during the first quarter of 1997.
Industrial output slipped to year-on-year 8.6 percent in January from 10.1 percent in December.

He expected Poland's official currency reserves, those held by the state, to fall to $17.8 billion in April from an estimated $18.2 at the end of January. He said net reserves, those in the entire banking system, would ease to $21.4 billion in April from about $21.5 in January.
